title_en: China Cinda Asset Management Co., Ltd., Lanzhou Office v. Gansu Yasheng Salt Chemical Industry (Group) Co., Ltd. — dispute over loan contract
ruling_gist_en: Where both parties to a contract agree that the contract shall become effective upon approval by the superior competent authority of one party, that party shall bear the obligation to promptly submit the contract to its superior competent authority for examination and approval, and to facilitate the entry into effect of the contract. If that party fails to perform the said contractual obligation, and the contract has been signed and sealed by both parties, its contents do not violate any prohibitive provisions of law, do not harm the interests of others, and have been partially performed, the contract shall be deemed to have become effective.
keywords_en: Civil; Loan contract dispute; Second instance; Supreme People's Court; Gansu Province; Legal person; Financial institution; Contract Law; Condition for contract effectiveness; Obligation of superior approval; Validity of debt restructuring agreement; Reversal of judgment; Loan contract; Debt restructuring; Assignment of claims; Merger; Good faith; Contract dispute; Loan contract dispute involving a limited liability company
full_text_en:
China Cinda Asset Management Company Lanzhou Office

v.

Gansu Yasheng Salt Chemical Industry (Group) Co., Ltd.

— Dispute over Loan Contract

Ruling Summary

Where the parties conclude a contract and stipulate that the approval of the superior competent authority of one party shall be a condition precedent for the contract to take effect, that party shall have the obligation to promptly submit the contract to its superior competent authority for examination and approval so as to cause the contract to take effect. Where that party neglects to perform the aforesaid contractual obligation, and the contract, having been signed and sealed by the parties, its contents violate no prohibitive provisions of law, cause no damage to the interests of others, and have been partially performed, it shall be determined that the contract has already taken effect.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2006) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 159

Appellant (original plaintiff of first instance): China Cinda Asset Management Company Lanzhou Office, domiciled at: No. 2 Unified Office Building, 77 Guangchang Nanlu, Lanzhou City, Gansu Province.

Responsible person: Chen Xinshu, Director of the Office.

Agent ad litem: Yu Xuehui, lawyer of Beijing Bihaode Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Liu Jianmin, lawyer of Beijing Bihaode Law Firm.

Respondent (original defendant of first instance): Gansu Yasheng Salt Chemical Industry (Group) Co., Ltd., domiciled at: No. 219, Zhangye Road, Chengguan District, Lanzhou City, Gansu Province.

Legal representative: Wang Dengfu, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Yang Jun, lawyer of Gansu Zhengtianhe Law Firm.

The Appellant, China Cinda Asset Management Company Lanzhou Office (hereinafter referred to as Cinda Lanzhou Office), being dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2005) Gan Min Er Chu Zi No. 56 rendered by the Gansu High People's Court in the case of a dispute over a loan contract with the Respondent, Gansu Yasheng Salt Chemical Industry (Group) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yasheng Group), appealed to this Court. After accepting the case, this Court lawfully formed a collegiate panel composed of trial judge Jia Wei as presiding judge, acting trial judges Sha Ling and Yuan Duoran to conduct the trial, with court clerk Yuan Hongxia keeping the record. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

The Gansu High People's Court found the following facts upon trial: Between 1990 and 1997, the Gansu Yanguoxia Chemical General Plant (hereinafter referred to as the Salt Chemical General Plant) and the China Construction Bank Yanguoxia Office (hereinafter referred to as the CCB Office) successively entered into six loan contracts. After reconciliation between the Salt Chemical General Plant and the CCB Office, as of September 20, 1999, the Salt Chemical General Plant owed the CCB Office a total of RMB 19,450,000 in loan principal and RMB 6,999,112.94 in interest, totaling RMB 26,449,112.94. In 1999, the CCB Office assigned all of the above claims to Cinda Lanzhou Office, and on November 11 of the same year notified the Salt Chemical General Plant of the assignment, which the Salt Chemical General Plant confirmed by affixing its seal on the notice receipt.

On July 16, 1999, Yasheng Group and the Salt Chemical General Plant entered into an acquisition agreement, whereby Yasheng Group would acquire the Salt Chemical General Plant by assuming its debts; the scope of acquisition included all assets, liabilities, and owners' equity; the effective date of the acquisition was the date the agreement was signed.

On November 20, 2000, the Salt Chemical General Plant, Yasheng Group, and Cinda Lanzhou Office entered into a tripartite Debt Restructuring Agreement stipulating: Cinda Lanzhou Office would conditionally reduce the debt owed by the Salt Chemical General Plant, with the reduced amount being RMB 16 million, the condition for the reduction being the timely repayment by the Salt Chemical General Plant, and Yasheng Group assuming joint and several liability for the original claim amount; if the Salt Chemical General Plant failed to perform or delayed performance of any installment repayment obligation, the debt reduction stipulated in the agreement would be invalidated, and full repayment would be required, and Cinda Lanzhou Office would have the right to require Yasheng Group to repay the unpaid original claim amount and the penalty interest corresponding to the principal portion of the original claim amount; the original claim amount was RMB 28,520,212.94, comprising principal of RMB 19,450,000 and interest of RMB 9,070,212.94 calculated up to September 20, 2000; Yasheng Group, as the guarantor under the agreement, assumed joint and several liability for the original claim; the guarantee period would be from the effective date of the agreement until the final installment under the new repayment plan was fully repaid; the guarantee liability of Yasheng Group could not be altered or terminated without authorization, and no conditions could be attached to the performance of the joint and several liability; the agreement would take effect upon being signed and sealed by the three parties and approved by China Cinda Asset Management Company (hereinafter referred to as Cinda Head Office). After the agreement was signed, Cinda Head Office approved it by reply on December 15 of the same year. Yasheng Group made payments of RMB 2 million on December 11 of the same year and December 30, 2001, respectively.

On December 26, 2002, the Salt Chemical General Plant, Yasheng Group, and Cinda Lanzhou Office entered into a tripartite Supplementary Debt Restructuring Agreement, confirming that after the original Debt Restructuring Agreement was signed, the Salt Chemical General Plant and Yasheng Group initially performed the agreement as agreed, repaying RMB 2 million in December 2000 and December 2001, respectively, totaling RMB 4 million in debt repayment. Thereafter, due to poor production and operation conditions of the Salt Chemical General Plant and other reasons, the Salt Chemical General Plant and Yasheng Group failed to implement the agreement as scheduled. The three parties negotiated and agreed: According to the tripartite debt restructuring agreement, as of December 25, 2002, the Salt Chemical General Plant owed Cinda Lanzhou Office RMB 12 million in matured debts; Cinda Lanzhou Office agreed to conditionally maintain the validity of the original Debt Restructuring Agreement, still reduce the original claim amount, with the reduced debt amount being RMB 12 million; the Salt Chemical General Plant and Yasheng Group agreed to repay the debt in cash and with the legal person shares of a listed company; cash of RMB 2 million was to be repaid before December 28, 2002, and the remaining RMB 10 million was to be offset with state-owned legal person shares of a listed company owned by Yasheng Group, with the transfer of the offsetting shares to be completed within 12 months; the condition for the reduction was the timely repayment of the agreed cash and the timely completion of the share transfer; if there was a delay in performance, the debt reduction stipulated in the agreement would be invalidated, and the Salt Chemical General Plant and Yasheng Group would be required to repay the full original claim amount, with the guarantee clauses in the original Debt Restructuring Agreement to be executed; if the offsetting shares could not be transferred on time, it would be deemed that the agreement could not be performed, and if negotiations failed, the cash repayment plan under the original Debt Restructuring Agreement would be executed; the agreement would take effect upon being signed and sealed by the three parties and approved by Cinda Head Office. After the agreement was signed, Yasheng Group paid RMB 2 million to Cinda Lanzhou Office on December 30 of the same year, but all other obligations remained unperformed.

In December 2003, Cinda Lanzhou Office and Yasheng Group entered into a Non-Performing Loan Claim Transfer Agreement stipulating: Yasheng Group agreed to acquire all of Cinda Lanzhou Office's claims against the Salt Chemical General Plant, totaling RMB 28,520,100; from the effective date of the formal contract signed by both parties, ancillary rights related to the subject matter of the transfer, including guarantee rights and mortgage rights, would also be transferred simultaneously; if relevant procedures were required by laws and regulations, such procedures should be handled, with costs borne by Yasheng Group; the overall transfer price was set at RMB 11.2 million; after deducting RMB 8 million paid before December 29, 2003, the remaining RMB 3.2 million was to be remitted in full to the account of Cinda Lanzhou Office within 10 days from the date of signing the agreement; the agreement would take effect upon being signed and sealed by both parties and approved by Cinda Head Office. After the agreement was signed, Yasheng Group paid RMB 2 million to Cinda Lanzhou Office, which amount was included in the RMB 8 million already paid, but both parties failed to perform the other obligations stipulated in the agreement.

On April 8, 2004, after discussions, Yasheng Group and Cinda Lanzhou Office signed a Meeting Minutes, the contents of which were identical to those of the Non-Performing Loan Claim Transfer Agreement.

It was also found that, on December 25, 2003, the Salt Chemical General Plant and Cinda Lanzhou Office signed a Debt Restructuring Property Mortgage Contract, stipulating that the Salt Chemical General Plant would mortgage certain property to Cinda Lanzhou Office and complete the mortgage registration procedures within 60 days. However, on January 8, 2004, the Salt Chemical General Plant was adjudicated bankrupt by the Yongjing County People's Court and entered into bankruptcy liquidation, and the parties did not complete the mortgage registration procedures. To recover the outstanding debts, Cinda Lanzhou Office filed a lawsuit with the Gansu High People's Court, requesting that Yasheng Group be ordered to immediately repay the loan of RMB 20,520,212.94 plus interest for delayed payment, and bear the litigation costs.

During the first instance trial, Cinda Lanzhou Office, in response to Yasheng Group's defense, argued that the Debt Restructuring Agreement had been approved by Cinda Head Office and was the only one of the three agreements that had taken effect. The subsequently signed Supplementary Debt Restructuring Agreement and Non-Performing Loan Claim Transfer Agreement were contracts subject to conditions precedent. Since any reduction of debt by Cinda Lanzhou Office of more than RMB 1 million required approval by Cinda Head Office, the Supplementary Debt Restructuring Agreement and Non-Performing Loan Claim Transfer Agreement had not been approved and therefore had not taken effect; both parties had not actually performed them, and Yasheng Group could not assert the defense of simultaneous performance. The mortgaged property agreed between Cinda Lanzhou Office and the Salt Chemical General Plant was property requiring mortgage registration; the parties agreed to complete the registration procedures within 60 days, but 10 days later, the Salt Chemical General Plant applied for bankruptcy to the Yongjing County People's Court of Gansu Province.

The Gansu High People's Court held that after Cinda Lanzhou Office acquired the claims from the CCB Office, the Debt Restructuring Agreement signed on November 20, 2000, with Yasheng Group and the Salt Chemical General Plant was a true expression of the parties' intent, and having been approved by Cinda Head Office, it satisfied the conditions for effectiveness stipulated in the contract and was a valid contract. Yasheng Group also performed part of its obligations under the contract. Thereafter, considering that the Salt Chemical General Plant had "failed to perform the agreement as scheduled due to poor production and operation conditions and other reasons," Cinda Lanzhou Office negotiated with the other parties, and on December 26, 2002, the three parties entered into the Supplementary Debt Restructuring Agreement, which also stipulated that approval by Cinda Lanzhou Office's superior department was a condition for the agreement to take effect. Yasheng Group paid RMB 2 million to Cinda Lanzhou Office under this agreement. In January 2004, due to the bankruptcy declaration of the Salt Chemical General Plant, the debt restructuring between Yasheng Group and the Salt Chemical General Plant failed. Cinda Lanzhou Office then entered into the Non-Performing Loan Claim Transfer Agreement with Yasheng Group in December 2003. The agreement stipulated an overall transfer price of RMB 11.2 million; after deducting RMB 8 million paid before December 29, 2003, the remaining balance was to be remitted in full to the account of Cinda Lanzhou Office within 10 days from the date of signing the agreement. The agreement again stipulated that it would take effect upon approval by Cinda Head Office. After the agreement was signed, Yasheng Group paid RMB 2 million to Cinda Lanzhou Office on December 30 of the same year. However, the other obligations agreed upon were not performed by either party. The Meeting Minutes of April 8, 2004, further clarified the above agreement.

Looking at the facts of this case, aside from the tripartite Debt Restructuring Agreement signed in 2000, which took effect upon the stipulated approval by Cinda Head Office, there was indeed no evidence that the Supplementary Debt Restructuring Agreement signed in 2002 and the Non-Performing Loan Claim Transfer Agreement signed in 2003 had been approved by Cinda Head Office, objectively making them contracts whose validity was pending. Cinda Lanzhou Office's argument that the Supplementary Debt Restructuring Agreement and the Non-Performing Loan Claim Transfer Agreement had not taken effect was valid. However, determining the rights and obligations of the parties solely based on the effective Debt Restructuring Agreement and supporting Cinda Lanzhou Office's claims would be manifestly unfair to Yasheng Group. First, in the context of contracts with pending validity, the party responsible for causing the contract to take effect should actively perform its obligations and should not, after obtaining benefits from the contract, later defend on the ground that the contract's validity is pending; doing so would violate the principle of good faith. Second, the evidence of Cinda Head Office's approval of the Debt Restructuring Agreement demonstrated that the obligation to submit for approval fell on Cinda Lanzhou Office, and Cinda Lanzhou Office had no evidence that its submission was not approved, nor any evidence that it informed Yasheng Group that the contract had not taken effect; the responsibility for the contract not taking effect could not be attributed to Yasheng Group. Third, considering Yasheng Group's performance of the contracts, it performed part of its obligations after each of the three agreements was signed; this payment behavior demonstrated that Yasheng Group believed that the conditions for the agreements to take effect might be fulfilled. Fourth, Yasheng Group performed part of its obligations under the "not yet effective" agreements, and Cinda Lanzhou Office actually realized part of its claims; it would be inequitable to then hold Yasheng Group liable under the Debt Restructuring Agreement. Therefore, Cinda Lanzhou Office's basis for claiming that the Supplementary Debt Restructuring Agreement and the Non-Performing Loan Claim Transfer Agreement had not taken effect and that Yasheng Group should bear repayment obligations under the Debt Restructuring Agreement was insufficient, and the court did not support it. The court, in accordance with Article 6 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment: Cinda Lanzhou Office's claims were dismissed. The first instance case acceptance fee of RMB 67,600 and the pre-litigation property preservation fee of RMB 51,300 were to be borne by Cinda Lanzhou Office.

Cinda Lanzhou Office, being dissatisfied with the aforementioned civil judgment of the Gansu High People's Court, appealed to this Court, stating: First, the trial court made errors in fact finding. 1. The Debt Restructuring Agreement signed on November 20, 2000, was an agreement whose effectiveness was conditional, a debt restructuring agreement providing for conditional debt reduction, and also a guarantee agreement in which Yasheng Group assumed guarantee liability in writing. The agreement stipulated conditions for debt reduction and also provided for the consequences in case of breach of those conditions. Yasheng Group's failure to repay the debt as agreed, breaching the conditions for debt reduction stipulated in the agreement, would not render the restructuring agreement invalid; it would merely invalidate the reduction clauses in the debt restructuring agreement, and Yasheng Group would still be required to perform its guarantee liability under the guarantee clauses of the agreement. 2. The Supplementary Debt Restructuring Agreement signed on December 26, 2002, did not invalidate the original Debt Restructuring Agreement. 3. The Non-Performing Loan Claim Transfer Agreement signed between Cinda Lanzhou Office and Yasheng Group in December 2003 was merely an intent-based draft agreement. It was evident from the Meeting Minutes of April 8, 2004, that the parties were still negotiating the agreement, and Yasheng Group had not performed any payment obligations under that agreement. 4. According to the "Measures for the Management of Asset Disposal by Financial Asset Management Companies" (hereinafter referred to as the "Asset Disposal Management Measures") promulgated by the Ministry of Finance on November 8, 2000, which stipulates: "Asset disposal plans involving asset disposal losses of RMB 1 million (inclusive) or more (calculated on a consolidated basis of all debts of a single debtor, the same below) must be reviewed and approved by the company's specialized asset disposal review body and then approved by the company's president." The agreement between Cinda Lanzhou Office and Yasheng Group was subject to approval by Cinda Head Office to take effect. Therefore, Articles 7 and 8 of the draft Non-Performing Loan Claim Transfer Agreement between Cinda Lanzhou Office and Yasheng Group clearly stipulated: "Yasheng Group shall pay RMB 3.2 million to Cinda Lanzhou Office within 10 days of signing the agreement. If this contract cannot be executed for any reason, the amount paid shall be received by Party A (Cinda Lanzhou Office) as repayment made by the Gansu Yanguoxia Chemical General Plant." Second, the trial court's application of law was improper. The Debt Restructuring Agreement between Yasheng Group and Cinda Lanzhou Office stipulated the assumption of joint and several guarantee liability, which should be confirmed in accordance with the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Guarantee Law). The guarantee period stipulated as "the guarantee period shall be from the effective date of this agreement until the final installment of the new repayment plan specified in this agreement is fully repaid" should, under the Guarantee Law, be deemed as an unclear stipulation; such guarantee period shall be two years from the date of maturity of the principal obligation. Therefore, the guarantee period for Yasheng Group as a joint and several guarantor should be two years from the date of maturity of the performance period stipulated in the Debt Restructuring Agreement, i.e., from December 20, 2003, to December 20, 2005. Yasheng Group should perform its joint and several guarantee liability in accordance with that agreement. In summary, the appellant requested that the original judgment be set aside, that Yasheng Group be ordered to repay Cinda Lanzhou Office the loan of RMB 20,520,212.94 plus interest for delayed payment, and that Yasheng Group bear the litigation costs of this case.

Yasheng Group argued in defense: After the Non-Performing Loan Claim Transfer Agreement was signed, Cinda Lanzhou Office neglected to perform the ancillary rights involved in the claim. The mortgage rights under the Debt Restructuring Property Mortgage Contract between Cinda Lanzhou Office and the Salt Chemical General Plant were not transferred to Yasheng Group due to Cinda Lanzhou Office's refusal to perform. Yasheng Group, in accordance with relevant legal provisions, refused to perform its obligation to pay the remaining amount. The Salt Chemical General Plant has now been declared bankrupt, and the portion of the mortgaged assets has been disposed of in accordance with relevant regulations, making it impossible for Yasheng Group to realize the mortgage rights it should have enjoyed; Cinda Lanzhou Office's conduct constitutes a breach of contract. The Non-Performing Loan Claim Transfer Agreement had already satisfied all conditions for the contract to take effect, and the parties had commenced performance, with Cinda Lanzhou Office also having accepted Yasheng Group's performance. The contract bore the characteristics of apparent authority and should be a valid contract. Cinda Lanzhou Office failed to perform its obligation to submit the Non-Performing Loan Claim Transfer Agreement for approval and also failed to inform Yasheng Group that the contract had not been approved. Even if the contract did not take effect, Cinda Lanzhou Office should bear pre-contractual liability. The three agreements involved in this case were new agreements reached by the parties, based on mutual agreement, to amend the relevant agreements. Once a new agreement took effect, the validity of the previous agreement was replaced by the new agreement, and the parties should perform their respective rights and obligations based on the contents of the Non-Performing Loan Claim Transfer Agreement. In summary, the original judgment was correct and should be upheld.

This Court found during the second instance trial that after the 2000 Debt Restructuring Agreement, the 2002 Supplementary Debt Restructuring Agreement, and the 2003 Non-Performing Loan Claim Transfer Agreement were signed, Cinda Head Office approved only the Debt Restructuring Agreement; the latter two agreements did not receive approval from Cinda Head Office. On November 8, 2000, the Ministry of Finance issued the Asset Disposal Management Measures to financial asset management companies by means of Cai Jin [2000] No. 122 Notice, Article 7 of which provides: "Asset disposal plans involving asset disposal losses of RMB 1 million (inclusive) or more (calculated on a consolidated basis of all debts of a single debtor, the same below) must be reviewed and approved by the company's specialized asset disposal review body and then approved by the company's president."

This Court holds: The focus of the dispute in this case is the determination of the validity of the Debt Restructuring Agreement, the Supplementary Debt Restructuring Agreement, and the Non-Performing Loan Claim Transfer Agreement, and the issue of the liability to be borne by Yasheng Group.

The debt that Yasheng Group should bear in this case originated from the merger agreement signed with the Salt Chemical General Factory under the method of assuming debt. Since the Salt Chemical General Factory has already been declared bankrupt, Xinda Lanzhou Office can only claim the creditor's rights against Yasheng Group. On November 20, 2000, the tripartite Debt Restructuring Agreement signed by Xinda Lanzhou Office, the Salt Chemical General Factory, and Yasheng Group primarily stipulated that the total debt of the Salt Chemical General Factory would be reduced to RMB 16 million, to be repaid in installments before December 20, 2003, with Yasheng Group assuming joint and several liability for the debt. The agreement was to take effect upon signature and seal by the three parties and approval by Xinda Head Office. On December 15 of the same year, Xinda Head Office approved the agreement. In December 2000 and December 2001, Yasheng Group paid RMB 2 million each time to Xinda Lanzhou Office, partially performing the agreed obligations under the agreement. Based on the above facts, the Debt Restructuring Agreement was reached through negotiation among the parties, reflecting their true intentions. Its content did not violate legal provisions and had been approved by Xinda Head Office, satisfying the conditions for the contract to take effect. Both parties had partially performed the agreement, so the agreement is lawful and valid. Due to the production and operation circumstances of the Salt Chemical General Factory and other reasons, Xinda Lanzhou Office only realized RMB 4 million of the creditor's rights, with RMB 12 million of overdue creditor's rights remaining. In December 2002, the three parties signed the Supplementary Debt Restructuring Agreement, further confirming the content of the Debt Restructuring Agreement. It stipulated that the Salt Chemical General Factory and Yasheng Group would repay RMB 2 million in cash by the 28th of that month, with the remaining RMB 10 million to be set off by the state-owned legal person shares of the listed company owned by Yasheng Group. If the shares used for debt setoff could not be transferred on time, repayment would still be made in cash. After the agreement was signed, Yasheng Group paid RMB 2 million to Xinda Lanzhou Office on the 30th of that month, but all other obligations remained unperformed. Since the content of the Supplementary Debt Restructuring Agreement was a confirmation and supplement to the Debt Restructuring Agreement, even though Xinda Head Office did not undergo the approval procedure for the Supplementary Debt Restructuring Agreement, its content did not exceed the scope of the Debt Restructuring Agreement that had already been approved by Xinda Head Office and had taken effect. Therefore, the Supplementary Debt Restructuring Agreement is lawful and valid.

Because the Salt Chemical General Factory entered bankruptcy proceedings, in December 2003, Xinda Lanzhou Office, together with Yasheng Group, signed the Non-performing Loan Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement based on the Debt Restructuring Agreement and the Supplementary Debt Restructuring Agreement. The parties agreed that Yasheng Group would acquire all of Xinda Lanzhou Office's creditor's rights against the Salt Chemical General Factory for RMB 11.2 million. After deducting the RMB 8 million already paid, the remaining RMB 3.2 million would be paid by Yasheng Group in a lump sum within 10 days. Xinda Lanzhou Office would transfer its mortgage security rights over the Salt Chemical General Factory to Yasheng Group. After signing the agreement, Yasheng Group paid another RMB 2 million to Xinda Lanzhou Office, bringing the total repayment of debt to Xinda Lanzhou Office to RMB 8 million, but the remaining RMB 3.2 million debt remained unperformed. However: First, the Debt Restructuring Agreement was signed after the issuance of the Asset Disposal Management Measures, and Xinda Head Office's approval of the Debt Restructuring Agreement should be based on the Asset Disposal Management Measures. The approval action of Xinda Head Office granted Xinda Lanzhou Office the authority to dispose of the Salt Chemical General Factory's debt. Second, Xinda Lanzhou Office is not an independent legal person but a branch of Xinda Head Office, responsible for disposing of Xinda Head Office's non-performing assets within Gansu Province. After Xinda Head Office approved the Debt Restructuring Agreement, Xinda Lanzhou Office obtained general authorization to dispose of the Salt Chemical General Factory's debt. Any agreement signed by Xinda Lanzhou Office in its own name relating to the disposal of the Salt Chemical General Factory's debt did not exceed the scope of such general authorization. Third, although the Non-performing Loan Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement reduced the Salt Chemical General Factory's debt from the RMB 16 million determined in the approved Debt Restructuring Agreement to RMB 11.2 million, the reduction amount reached the RMB 1 million reporting threshold stipulated in the Asset Disposal Management Measures. However, since the Asset Disposal Management Measures are a departmental regulation issued by the Ministry of Finance for asset management companies, not a regulation applicable to all entities in the market economy, nor a mandatory provision of law, the Non-performing Loan Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement cannot be deemed not to have taken effect solely based on that regulation. It must also be determined whether the asset management company has completed internal approval procedures or should have completed such procedures. Fourth, although the Non-performing Loan Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement stipulated the condition that it would take effect upon approval by Xinda Head Office, since the approval procedure is an internal process between Xinda Head Office and its branch Xinda Lanzhou Office, and the agreement imposed an obligation on Xinda Lanzhou Office to unilaterally procure the contract's effectiveness, Xinda Lanzhou Office must not delay in submitting for approval or even fail to submit for approval in violation of the agreement to counter the counterparty and prevent the agreement from taking legal effect. If one party neither performs its contractual obligations nor permits a contract with pending effectiveness to become effective due to internal procedures, thereby obtaining greater benefits after the contract fails to take effect, this would place the counterparty in an unfavorable position. Particularly in this case, after Xinda Lanzhou Office had already obtained general authorization to dispose of the Salt Chemical General Factory's debt, and based on the Debt Restructuring Agreement and the Supplementary Debt Restructuring Agreement, it entered into the Non-performing Loan Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement with Yasheng Group only after the Salt Chemical General Factory had entered bankruptcy proceedings. Therefore, Xinda Lanzhou Office should have actively applied to Xinda Head Office. Even if Xinda Head Office did not approve, it should have timely notified Yasheng Group. However, from the signing of the agreement in December 2003 to the filing of the lawsuit in October 2005, a period of nearly two years, Xinda Lanzhou Office did not notify Yasheng Group whether it had submitted for approval to Xinda Head Office or whether approval had been obtained. Fifth, the Non-performing Loan Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement was negotiated and signed by both parties. Its content did not violate legal provisions or harm the legitimate rights and interests of others, and Yasheng Group had partially performed the agreement by paying an additional RMB 2 million. In summary, when a contract takes effect subject to an internal condition of one party, and the party obligated to facilitate the contract's effectiveness fails to perform that obligation, then where the contract content does not violate mandatory legal provisions or harm others' interests, has been signed and sealed by both parties, and has been partially performed, the contract should be deemed to have taken effect. Xinda Lanzhou Office's appeal argument that the Non-performing Loan Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement was merely a non-binding draft agreement and, not having been approved by Xinda Head Office, had no legal effect, is inconsistent with the facts and its own obligations, and this Court does not support it.

Xinda Lanzhou Office contends that the Supplementary Debt Restructuring Agreement and the Non-performing Loan Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement were contracts subject to a condition precedent. Because they were not approved by Xinda Head Office, they did not take legal effect. Therefore, it sued Yasheng Group based on the Debt Restructuring Agreement, seeking a judgment ordering Yasheng Group to repay the remaining total debt of the original Salt Chemical General Factory of RMB 20,522,012.94 and interest, after deducting the RMB 8 million already paid. Although Xinda Lanzhou Office's claims were not based on the Non-performing Loan Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement, its claims included the debt that Yasheng Group should bear. Therefore, this Court's adjudication of the creditor-debtor relationship between Xinda Lanzhou Office and Yasheng Group based on the Non-performing Loan Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement does not exceed the scope of Xinda Lanzhou Office's claims. Yasheng Group's defense that the Non-performing Loan Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement had already satisfied all conditions for the contract to take effect is supported by this Court. The bankruptcy of the Salt Chemical General Factory resulted in the failure to transfer the mortgaged assets stipulated in the Non-performing Loan Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement to Xinda Lanzhou Office, thereby failing to achieve the contractual purpose of transferring the mortgage security rights to Yasheng Group. Since this fact was not determined by Xinda Lanzhou Office's will, and because the Non-performing Loan Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement had warned Yasheng Group of the risks associated with the purchased creditor's rights, Yasheng Group cannot rely on the failure to realize the mortgage security rights to oppose its obligations under the Non-performing Loan Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement. Therefore, this Court does not support Yasheng Group's defense request that it should not bear the remaining debt and that the original judgment should be upheld.

In summary, the original trial's determination that the Supplementary Debt Restructuring Agreement and the Non-performing Loan Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement had not taken effect was improper, and the judgment dismissing Xinda Lanzhou Office's claims was erroneous. This Court hereby corrects that error. Pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Items (2) and (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court renders the following judgment:

1. The civil judgment (2005) Gan Min Er Chu Zi No. 56 of the Gansu Higher People's Court is vacated;

2. Gansu Yasheng Salt Chemical Industry (Group) Co., Ltd. shall pay China Cinda Asset Management Co., Ltd., Lanzhou Office, the principal amount of RMB 3.2 million and interest thereon (calculated from January 10, 2004, to the date of payment at the overdue loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period).

The above payment shall be made within fifteen days from the date of service of this judgment. In case of overdue payment, the interest for delayed performance shall be doubled. The period for China Cinda Asset Management Co., Ltd., Lanzhou Office, to apply for compulsory execution is six months from the date of receipt of this judgment.

The first instance case acceptance fee of RMB 67,600 and the pre-litigation preservation fee of RMB 51,300, totaling RMB 118,900, shall be borne by Gansu Yasheng Salt Chemical Industry (Group) Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 23,780 and by China Cinda Asset Management Co., Ltd., Lanzhou Office in the amount of RMB 95,120. The second instance case acceptance fee of RMB 67,600 shall be borne by Gansu Yasheng Salt Chemical Industry (Group) Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 13,520 and by China Cinda Asset Management Co., Ltd., Lanzhou Office in the amount of RMB 54,080.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Jia Wei

Acting Judge: Sha Ling
